seoDescription: Master Phasmophobia's ultimate challenge with this comprehensive no-evidence guide. Learn to identify every ghost, from the Spirit and Wraith to the Deogen and Thaye, by understanding their unique behaviors and hidden traits. This tutorial covers everything you need to know, including hunt patterns, special abilities, and specific tests using items like smudge sticks and salt. Elevate your gameplay and conquer any contract by learning to differentiate ghosts like the Oni and Phantom by hunt visibility alone.

summary:
## Phasmophobia No-Evidence Identification Guide

This guide outlines the unique tells and behaviors for identifying every ghost in Phasmophobia without collecting official evidence.

### ## Spirit
- **Test**: Smudge the ghost and time how long it takes to hunt again.
- **Behavior**: A **Spirit** is prevented from hunting for **3 minutes** after being smudged, double the standard 90-second duration for most other ghosts.

### ## Wraith
- **Test**: Place lines of **salt**.
- **Behavior**: The **Wraith** is the only ghost that will not step in or disturb salt piles. It leaves no footprints.

### ## Phantom
- **Test 1**: Take a picture of the ghost during a ghost event.
- **Behavior**: A **Phantom** will be invisible in the photo, though the picture will still register as a "Ghost Photo" in the journal.
- **Test 2**: Observe its visibility during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: A **Phantom** blinks much slower and is less visible than other ghosts during a hunt.

### ## Poltergeist
- **Test 1**: Observe object interactions.
- **Behavior**: Can throw multiple objects at once, known as a **"Polty bomb"**.
- **Test 2**: Observe object interactions during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: Throws objects more frequently (every 0.5 seconds) and with more force than other ghosts.

### ## Banshee
- **Test**: Use a **Parabolic Microphone**.
- **Behavior**: Has a unique vocalization, the **Banshee Wail**, which has a 33% chance of being heard on the parabolic microphone.

### ## Jinn
- **Test**: Trigger a hunt with the **breaker on**.
- **Behavior**: A **Jinn** will accelerate to a high speed when it has line of sight on a player who is more than 3 meters away. It slows to normal speed once it gets closer.
> [!IMPORTANT]
> This ability only works if the building's breaker is on.

### ## Mare
- **Test 1**: Observe light switch interactions.
- **Behavior**: A **Mare** can **never** turn a light on.
- **Test 2**: Flip a light switch on near the ghost.
- **Behavior**: Has an ability to instantly turn a light switch off moments after a player turns it on.

### ## Revenant
- **Test**: Observe its speed during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: Moves very slowly when it has no line of sight. Upon seeing a player or detecting their active electronics, it becomes extremely fast.

### ## Shade
- **Test 1**: Use a cursed possession to force a ghost event (e.g., Summoning Circle, Music Box).
- **Behavior**: It's the only ghost that can appear in **shadow form** for these events.
- **Test 2**: Stay in the ghost room.
- **Behavior**: A **Shade** is shy and will not perform hunts or interactions if a player is in the same room.

### ## Demon
- **Test 1**: Monitor sanity and hunt times.
- **Behavior**: Can initiate a hunt at **any sanity level** without a cursed item.
- **Test 2**: Smudge the ghost and time the hunt delay.
- **Behavior**: Can hunt just **60 seconds** after being smudged, as opposed to the standard 90 seconds.

### ## Yurei
- **Test**: Observe door interactions.
- **Behavior**: A **Yurei** can only ever fully open or fully shut a door, never partially.

### ## Oni
- **Test 1**: Watch for ghost events.
- **Behavior**: The **Oni** cannot perform the misty-breath "air ball" ghost event.
- **Test 2**: Observe its visibility during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: It is **more visible** than a standard ghost, blinking less frequently during hunts (the opposite of a Phantom).

### ## Yokai
- **Test**: Use your voice or active electronics during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: A **Yokai** has very poor hearing and can only detect players' voices and equipment within a **2.5-meter range** during a hunt.

### ## Hantu
- **Test**: Turn the breaker off and initiate a hunt.
- **Behavior**: A **Hantu** is the only ghost that will emit visible **freezing breath** from its mouth during a hunt in a cold environment (breaker off).
> [!NOTE]
> A Hantu can never turn the breaker on.

### ## Goryo
- **Test**: Track the ghost's location over time.
- **Behavior**: A **Goryo** will **never** change its favorite room.
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Do not confuse roaming with a permanent room change. This makes the Goryo very difficult to identify and is usually confirmed by ruling out other ghosts.

### ## Myling
- **Test**: Listen for its footsteps during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: A **Myling's** footsteps are much quieter and are only audible within **12 meters**, compared to the standard 20 meters for other ghosts.

### ## Onryo
- **Test**: Use candles or lighters.
- **Behavior**: An **Onryo** cannot hunt if a lit flame is within 4 meters of it. After extinguishing its third flame, it will attempt to hunt regardless of sanity. A nearby flame will act as a crucifix, being extinguished to prevent the hunt.

### ## The Twins
- **Test**: Listen to footstep speed during multiple hunts.
- **Behavior**: Hunts can be initiated by either a "fast twin" (10% faster than normal) or a "slow twin" (10% slower than normal).

### ## Raiju
- **Test**: Place an active electronic item on the floor during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: A **Raiju** moves at normal speed but will significantly speed up when it is near active player electronics.

### ## Obake
- **Test**: Observe the ghost model during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: The **Obake** has a chance to **shapeshift** into a different ghost model during its blinks. It will not switch between male and female models.

### ## The Mimic
- **Test**: Look for **Ghost Orbs** with a video camera in a no-evidence game.
- **Behavior**: The **Mimic** is the only ghost that will show Ghost Orbs on a zero-evidence contract, as orbs are a forced trait, not a piece of evidence for it.

### ## Moroi
- **Test 1**: Track its speed as average sanity drops.
- **Behavior**: A **Moroi's** speed is directly linked to average player sanity; it gets progressively faster as sanity decreases, becoming the fastest ghost at 0% sanity.
- **Test 2**: Smudge the ghost during a hunt.
- **Behavior**: The smudge stick effect lasts for **7.5 seconds** on a Moroi, 50% longer than the standard 5 seconds.

### ## Deogen
- **Test**: Get it to hunt.
- **Behavior**: A **Deogen** always knows the player's location. It moves extremely fast from a distance but slows to a crawl when it gets very close, making it easy to loop.

### ## Thaye
- **Test 1**: Track its speed over multiple hunts.
- **Behavior**: A **Thaye** "ages" when players are nearby, causing it to become slower with each subsequent hunt.
- **Test 2**: Use the Ouija board.
- **Behavior**: Asking the Ouija board for its age multiple times throughout a match will show its age increasing.
transcription:
## Introduction & Identifying the Spirit

By the end of this video, you're going to know how to identify every single ghost with no evidence in Phasmophobia. It doesn't matter if you're a beginner or an experienced player. I'm going to teach you everything you need to know about each ghost to successfully complete your no evidence games. Let's get right into it and let's start it off strong with the Spirit.

To test for a Spirit on no evidence, you want to smudge the ghost and start a timer immediately when you do so. Spirits are not able to hunt again until waiting a minimum time of 3 minutes after being smudged. Every other ghost except for Demon has to wait a minimum of 1 minute and 30 seconds after being smudged, meaning that Spirits have to wait double the time than every other ghost. So what this means is that if your ghost hunts before your timer hits 3 minutes, then you can safely rule out Spirit. However, if your ghost keeps waiting until 3 minutes pass after being smudged to hunt again, it's most likely a Spirit. Spirit can hunt starting right now. Okay.

## Identifying the Wraith

Next up, let's talk about the Wraith. Wraiths are super easy to identify with no evidence. To test for a Wraith on no evidence, all you need to do is put down salt. When walking over salt, Wraiths will just walk over it and won't disturb it, leave any imprints or footprints.

## Identifying the Phantom

The next ghost that we're talking about is a Phantom. Phantoms are also extremely easy to identify with no evidence. One of the ways that you can identify a Phantom is by taking a photo of it during a ghost event. They will disappear and will not appear inside of the ghost photo in the journal. However, the photo will still be labeled as a ghost photo.

The second way to identify a Phantom is during a hunt. Phantoms are less visible than any other ghost when hunting and will disappear for longer in between blinks. This is an example of a normal ghost during a hunt and a Phantom during a hunt.

## Identifying the Poltergeist

Moving on, next we have the Poltergeist. Poltergeists are very fun to identify with no evidence, and you can do it in two different ways. Poltergeists are the only ghosts in the game that have an ability to throw multiple objects at once. This is known as a Polty bomb. There are four different variants of the Polty bomb, and this is what they look like.

You can also identify a Poltergeist during a hunt as they will throw objects every 0.5 seconds. You'll notice that these throws are more powerful than any other ghost.

## Identifying the Banshee

Next up, let's talk about the Banshee. Banshees can be identified using a parabolic microphone as it has its own unique sound called the Banshee wail that it can give you when using the parabolic microphone. It has a 33% chance to give this audio when listening with the parabolic microphone and there's 20 different variants, but they all sound very similar. Here's an example of what a few of them sound like.

## Identifying the Jinn

Up next, let's talk about the Jinn. Jinn has an interesting ability that is dependent on if the breaker is turned on or if it's turned off. If the breaker is turned off, the Jinn will move at normal speed when it has line of sight on you. However, if the breaker is on, the Jinn will speed up if it has line of sight on you and is further than 3m away. Once the Jinn is less than 3m away from you, it'll slow back down to normal speed. This is an example of what this ability looks like.

## Identifying the Mare

Next up, we have the Mare. Mares cannot turn on lights, meaning if your ghost turns on a light switch or a lamp, you can immediately rule out Mare. Mares also can be identified only using a light switch. The Mare has an ability where it can immediately flick a light switch back to its off position that you just turned on if it is within four meters of the ghost. This is what that looks like.

## Identifying the Revenant

Next up, let's talk about the Revenant. Revenants are one of the scariest ghosts in the game, but they are one of the easiest to identify without evidence. When it's hunting, the Revenant will move at a very slow pace if it does not have any line of sight or detect any players nearby with electronics on. However, once the Revenant gains line of sight on a player or detects a player nearby with electronics on, it will move at a very fast speed until it loses line of sight again or if it loses detection of that player. Here's an example of these two speeds.

## Identifying the Shade

Up next, we're talking about the Shade. Shades are probably the most boring ghost to identify on no evidence. However, you can go about identifying Shades in a couple different ways on no evidence. Starting off with the first way, Shades are the only ghost in the game that can appear in shadow form when using the summoning circle, music box, or monkey paw for a ghost event. And the last way to identify a Shade on no evidence is through ghost hunt and interactions. The Shade is unable to do any ghost hunt or interactions with you standing inside of the same room as the ghost. This includes the ghost blowing out firelights. So, what this means is that if you find that your ghost is not doing anything with you inside of the room, but once you step out of the ghost room, it becomes active, then it is a Shade.

## Identifying the Demon

Moving on to one of the deadliest ghosts in the game, let's talk about the Demon. Demons are the only ghost in the game that have the ability to hunt you at any time, regardless of how high your sanity is. The Demon is also the only ghost in the game that is able to hunt at 60 seconds after being smudged instead of the normal 1 minute and 30 seconds that every other ghost besides from the Spirit has to wait. So, if you start a timer after smudging the ghost, and your ghost hunts before 1 minute and 30 seconds go by, it is a Demon.

## Identifying the Yurei

Next up, we have the Yurei. Yureis when they get smudged, enter something called a favorite room state, where it is unable to leave its favorite room for 90 seconds. The best way to identify a Yurei though on no evidence is with its door ability. The Yurei when interacting with doors outside of a hunt can only fully open them or fully close them. So if your ghost does a door interaction that doesn't result in a fully open or fully closed door, you can roll out Yurei.

## Identifying the Oni

Next up, let's talk about the Oni. Onis cannot do mist ghost events. So if your ghost does one, you can safely roll out an Oni. The only way to identify an Oni on no evidence though is through a hunt. The Oni is opposite of a Phantom during a hunt, meaning that it is more visible when blinking than the normal ghost. This is an example of what a normal ghost looks like during a hunt and what an Oni looks like during a hunt.

## Identifying the Yokai

Next up, let's talk about the Yokai. Yokai are unable to detect you talking or your electronics unless they are within 2.5 meters of you during a hunt. You can use your radio to test if it's a Yokai during a hunt. Hold down your radio button and if there is static and the ghost doesn't come to your position, it is a Yokai. I'll show you an example.

## Identifying the Hantu

Up next, let's talk about the Hantu. Hantus are unable to turn on the breaker, meaning that if your ghost does turn on the breaker, you can immediately roll out a Hantu. However, the easiest way to identify a Hantu without any evidence is to turn off the breaker and then get the ghost to hunt. Hantus will have freezing breath coming from the ghost model's mouth during a hunt with the breaker off. This is the only ghost that has this effect, and I'll show you an example of it right now.

## Identifying the Goryo

Now, let's move on to the most annoying ghost on no evidence to identify, the Goryo. Goryos are basically impossible to identify when playing with no evidence unless you've already ruled out every other ghost. The only trait that you can use for no evidence with the Goryo is that Goryos are unable to change their favorite room location during the contract. What this means is that if your ghost changes its favorite room during the game, you can safely rule out Goryo. However, make sure you don't confuse this with the ghost just roaming out of its room.

## Identifying the Myling

Moving on to the Myling. Mylings can be identified either with a parabolic microphone or based on the volume of their footsteps during a hunt. Myling is the only ghost in the game that can give two parabolic responses within 80 seconds of each other. However, most people choose to identify it during a hunt. Myling's footsteps and vocals can only be heard from 12 meters away compared to the normal 20 meters away, making them silent and deadly. This is a comparison between a Myling and a normal ghost during a hunt.

## Identifying the Onryo

Next up, let's talk about the Onryo. Onryos can be identified using candles. Onryos cannot hunt if there is a lit candle within 4 meters of the ghost. So, you can basically use candles as a crucifix with Onryo. Additionally, the Onryo will also attempt to hunt at any sanity after extinguishing every third flame. However, if there is another lit candle nearby when the Onryo attempts to hunt, the flame will prevent the hunt and act as a crucifix, and the Onryo will blow it out. This is what that looks like.

## Identifying The Twins

Next up, let's talk about the Twins. The twins can be identified through the speed of the ghost during a hunt. Because the twins have two different speeds it can choose from when starting a hunt. It will either choose between the fast twin, which is 10% faster than normal ghost speed, or the slow twin, which is 10% slower than normal ghost speed. It is a random chance on which one you'll get each hunt. This is what those two different speeds will sound like and how it compares to a normal ghost during a hunt.

## Identifying the Raiju

Next up, let's talk about the Raiju. Raiju can be identified by their speed during a hunt. A Raiju will move at normal ghost speed unless it comes within range of active player electronic equipment that is turned on. Then it will drastically speed up. This is an example.

## Identifying the Obake

Next up, let's talk about the Obake. Obake can shapeshift into different models during hunts. However, if your ghost is a male, it will not turn into a female model. And if your ghost is a female, it will not turn into a male model. This is an example of an Obake shapeshift.

## Identifying The Mimic

Next up, let's talk about the Mimic. The Mimic is the easiest ghost to identify on zero evidence. This is because the Mimic is the only ghost that will give you a fake piece of evidence on zero evidence. You can identify Mimic using a video camera because the Mimic will still give orbs on zero evidence. This is because orbs is one of his traits and not an actual piece of evidence. So if you see ghost orbs on zero evidence, it is 100% a Mimic.

## Identifying the Moroi

Next up, let's talk about Moroi. Moroi will change its speed during a hunt depending on the group's average sanity. Moroi will be slower than the average ghost when your sanity is higher. However, when you hit 50% average sanity, the Moroi will start to speed up during hunts. The Moroi is fastest when the average sanity is at 0%. When you smudge a Moroi during a hunt, it will also last longer than it would on any other ghost. Typically, smudging the ghost during a hunt only lasts for 5 seconds, but with Moroi, it is increased by 50% and will last for a total of seven and a half seconds.

## Identifying the Deogen

Next up, let's talk about the Deogen. Deogens are very deadly if you're unaware that you're dealing with one. However, they are very easy to survive and identify. Deogens will constantly track your location, so there is no hiding from them. From a distance, they are very fast, but when they get closer to you, they will slow down to a very slow speed. You are able to loop the ghost very easily at this speed. This is what a Deogen hunt looks like.

## Identifying the Thaye & Conclusion

Moving on to the last ghost that we're going to be talking about, the Thaye. You can identify this ghost during a hunt or using a Ouija board. Thaye is the only ghost that will age during a contract if you're standing in the ghost room. When a Thaye ages, it will get slower and slower each hunt. It does not have any line of sight speed up, so it is very easy to loop it as the game goes on. If you want to identify it using a Ouija board, simply ask the Ouija board how old the ghost is, then go stand in the ghost room for a few minutes. Once a few minutes have passed, return to the Ouija board and once again ask it how old the ghost is. If the age has changed and it is now older, it is a Thaye.

And that will conclude this no evidence guide. Let me know if this video helped you. And if it did, consider subscribing and joining the Discord in the description. And if you enjoy live content, I do stream on Twitch multiple times a week. Let me know which ghost is your favorite to identify on Zero Evidence.
